title: A five-minute pause
description: A gentle reflection for an ordinary day. A notebook is optional.

body.heading: Arrive as you are
paragraphs: This is an optional writing prompt, not a test. Choose a comfortable place and give yourself about five minutes if you have them. Keep your eyes open or simply look around. You can stop whenever you want.
Start with one neutral observation: the colour of a wall, the sound of a passing car, or the feeling of a cup in your hand. You do not need to achieve a particular mood.

body.heading: Ask three small questions
paragraphs: What caught my attention today? Write a sentence about something specific, however ordinary. A conversation, a sentence in a book, or a patch of light is enough.
What took more effort than I expected? Name the task without turning it into a judgment about yourself. Then ask: what is one thing I would like to carry into tomorrow?

body.heading: Choose what to keep
paragraphs: Read back only if you want to. Circle one phrase, close the notebook, or leave the page unfinished. There is no score and no correct answer.

This reflection offers a structure for thinking, not a health outcome. If reflecting feels unhelpful, choose a different activity or leave it for another day. Nothing needs to be entered on this website.

takeaway: Notice one thing, name one effort, and choose one thought to carry forward.
